body: **Review record** from `review-points.md` (4 read-only Sonnet reviewers (correctness, security, ticket-fit, tests) + CI/SonarCloud): 5 auto-fixed · 9 declined and still open · 8 assumptions. Each open one is on the line it is about, or quoted below with its lines when that line is not in the diff.

comments.title: A huge page overflowed the int offset into a 500
comments.anchor: return requested == null ? 0 : Math.clamp(requested, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE / pageSize);
comments.body:
**Auto-fixed** — A huge page overflowed the int offset into a 500

**Reviewer:** `page` was clamped only to Integer.MAX_VALUE, so `page × size` overflowed the int offset JPA takes and `?page=2147483647&size=20` threw a 500 instead of serving the last page.

**Fix:** cap the page at `Integer.MAX_VALUE / size`, and clamp the size into [5, 20] before snapping so a huge negative size cannot overflow either.

<sub>raised by correctness, security and tests reviewers</sub>

comments.title: navigate() promise left floating
comments.body:
**Auto-fixed** — navigate() promise left floating

**Reviewer:** `router.navigate` returns a promise nobody handled; Sonar rates it a BUG and the quality gate fails on it.

**Fix:** mark it explicitly ignored with `void`.

**Reviewer:** each column's test only checked that the 10 rows shown were in order, so a sort applied to the page instead of the table would still pass.

**Fix:** each case also asserts the first row is the global extreme of that column.

comments.title: Owner column sorts by first name, then last name
comments.body:
**Assumption** · confidence 0.60 — Owner column sorts by first name, then last name

**Not taken:** last name first, the usual directory order

**Why:** the column shows "First Last", so this order reads sorted on screen and lets the acceptance test compare the visible text. A clinic may still expect surname order, which keeps it near a coin flip.

comments.title: A size equidistant from two allowed sizes snaps down
comments.body:
**Assumption** · confidence 0.50 — A size equidistant from two allowed sizes snaps down

**Not taken:** 15 snaps up to 20

**Why:** "nearest" leaves the tie open; the stream takes the first, smaller size. Nobody types 15, so it barely matters.

comments.title: An unreadable page number serves the first page
comments.anchor: return requested == null ? 0 : Math.clamp(requested, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE / pageSize);
comments.body:
**Assumption** · confidence 0.75 — An unreadable page number serves the first page

**Not taken:** treat it as past the end and serve the last page

**Why:** Q3 names only "past the end"; garbage reads closest to "no page given", which defaults to the first.

comments.title: Page, size and sort live in the URL query
comments.body:
**Assumption** · confidence 0.80 — Page, size and sort live in the URL query

**Not taken:** component state only, lost on reload

**Why:** a reload or Back keeps the front desk's place. It is not asked for, but it is cheap and fits Angular routing.

comments.title: The response echoes the sort it actually applied
comments.body:
**Assumption** · confidence 0.85 — The response echoes the sort it actually applied

**Not taken:** the client trusts the sort it asked for

**Why:** after a fallback the header arrows must show the order actually served; the echo is built only from our own constants.
